title: Verdier biduality over a finite coefficient field
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ (separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion, and finite type means its structure morphism has finite type) [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use the derived-complete integral constructible categories [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] and their raw rationalizations $D^b_c(X,E)$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. For each finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, put $R=\mathcal O_E$ and let $D_{X,R}=R\mathcal Hom_R(-,\omega_{X,R})$ be integral duality [thm-coef-integral-verdier], with the integral dualizing object of [prop-coef-integral-dualizing]. Then integral duality induces an exact $E$-linear anti-equivalence
$$D_{X,E}:D^b_c(X,E)^{\mathrm{op}}\xrightarrow{\sim}D^b_c(X,E).$$
Its evaluation and natural isomorphism $\delta_K:K\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{X,E}D_{X,E}K$ are obtained by rationalizing integral evaluation and biduality. The dualizing object is the image $\omega_{X,E}$ of $\omega_{X,R}$. Tensor products and evaluation at the rational stage use the coefficient-passage operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], with completed derived tensor at the integral stage. For finite coefficient-field extensions $E\subset L$, the rationalization of the canonical integral comparison [lem-coef-integral-finite-extension] is a natural isomorphism
$$(D_{X,E}K)\otimes_E L\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{X,L}(K\otimes_E L),$$
commuting with evaluation and $\delta$, and satisfying the unit and associator equations for scalar extension.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C_R=D^b_c(X,R)$ and $D_R=D_{X,R}$. By [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor], every object of this actual integral category belongs to its finite-Tor subcategory: $\ell$ is invertible on the $k$-scheme $X$, so the lemma applies. The integral theorem [thm-coef-integral-verdier] gives an exact anti-equivalence $D_R:\mathcal C_R^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C_R$, and its actual double-dual map is invertible. The object $\omega_{X,R}$ belongs to $\mathcal C_R$ by [prop-coef-integral-dualizing]. The internal Hom construction in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] is $R$-linear on morphisms in its first, contravariant variable: precomposition satisfies $h\circ(rf)=r(h\circ f)$, so $D_R(rf)=rD_R(f)$, also on the derived internal Hom. Thus no involution on scalars occurs.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1: domain of integral duality and its scalar linearity; explicit expansion

proof.text:
Let $Q_R:\mathcal C_R\to\mathcal C_R[1/\varpi_E]$ be [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]; this is $D^b_c(X,E)$ by [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Define $D_EK=D_RK$ on objects and $D_E(f\otimes a)=D_R(f)\otimes a$. The balancing relation is preserved since $D_R(rf)\otimes a=D_R(f)\otimes ra$. For $f:K\to M$, $g:M\to N$, the two formulas for a composite give
$$D_E((g\otimes b)(f\otimes a))=D_R(f)D_R(g)\otimes ab=(D_R(f)\otimes a)(D_R(g)\otimes b).$$
Identities go to identities; additivity extends these equations to sums of tensors. This defines an $E$-linear contravariant functor on the prescribed raw localization, including any torsion identifications imposed by the tensor product. It also identifies $(\mathcal C_R^{\mathrm{op}})[1/\varpi_E]$ with $(\mathcal C_R[1/\varpi_E])^{\mathrm{op}}$: both have Hom module $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_R}(M,K)\otimes_R E$ and the same reversed composition. No application of a transport theorem outside its stated category is needed.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 1-2: explicit tensor balancing, reversed composition, and opposite identification

proof.text: The exactness assertion follows on the specified triangulations. By [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], every distinguished rational triangle is isomorphic to $Q_R(T)$ for an integral distinguished triangle $T$. Apply the integral exact contravariant functor of [thm-coef-integral-verdier] to $T$ and then $Q_R$; the resulting reversed triangle is distinguished, and is precisely the $D_E$-image with its localized integral shift comparison. That comparison is invertible because its integral inverse also localizes. Images of the triangle isomorphism remain isomorphisms, proving exactness for every rational triangle.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1: exactness of the contravariant extension, expanded using localized triangles

proof.text: For $K,M\in\mathcal C_R$, integral anti-equivalence [thm-coef-integral-verdier] makes $f\mapsto D_R(f)$ an $R$-linear bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(K,M)\to\operatorname{Hom}(D_RM,D_RK)$. Its inverse is $R$-linear (apply the bijection to sums and scalar multiples); tensoring both maps with $E$ leaves their composites equal to the identities. By the Hom formula in [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], these are the Hom maps of $D_E$ and their inverses. Thus $D_E$ is fully faithful. Every object $K$ is isomorphic to $D_E(D_EK)$ by $Q_R(\delta_K)$, with inverse $Q_R(\delta_K^{-1})$, so it is essentially surjective and hence an anti-equivalence. The natural integral transformation $\delta:\mathrm{id}\to D_R^2$ extends by [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport], applied only to the covariant exact endofunctors $\mathrm{id},D_R^2$ of the integral category. Explicitly, $D_E^2(f\otimes a)(\delta_K\otimes1)=(\delta_M\otimes1)(f\otimes a)$ is integral naturality tensored with $a$. This proves naturality and invertibility of the claimed actual double-dual map, not just existence of some isomorphism.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3, first three sentences: Hom inverse, essential surjectivity, and canonical natural biduality

proof.text:
The rational tensor is the localization of the completed integral tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Its integral source remains in $\mathcal C_R$ by [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible], applied with $f=\mathrm{id}_X$. Therefore define $\omega_{X,E}=Q_R\omega_{X,R}$ and $\mathrm{ev}_{E,K}=Q_R(\mathrm{ev}_{R,K})$, using integral evaluation supplied by [thm-coef-integral-verdier]. The integral evaluation naturality equation for $f:K\to M$ is
$$\mathrm{ev}_{R,K}(D_R(f)\widehat\otimes1_K)=\mathrm{ev}_{R,M}(1_{D_RM}\widehat\otimes f).$$
After applying $Q_R$, the equation for $f\otimes a$ is this same equality multiplied by $a$, because tensor and duality act linearly in each variable. Sums give naturality for all rational morphisms. The double-dual map is $\delta_{E,K}=Q_R\delta_{R,K}$ from step 4: the integral transpose/evaluation defining equality is an equality of composites of evaluation, tensor, and identities, so its image is the same defining equality for the localized maps. This verifies the asserted rationalization of evaluation and its transpose.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3, fourth sentence: completed tensor, evaluation, and transpose localization

proof.text:
For $E\subset L$ let $S=\mathcal O_L$ and $T=T_{S/R}$. The exact functor $T$, the dualizing comparison $u:T\omega_{X,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{X,S}$ and the natural duality comparison $\beta_K:TD_RK\xrightarrow{\sim}D_STK$, with their inverses, are supplied by [lem-coef-integral-finite-extension]. Define the rational comparison to be $Q_S(\beta_K)$. Its source and target are exactly those stated: [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] defines $-\otimes_E L$ by $K\mapsto TK$ and $f\otimes a\mapsto T(f)\otimes a$, with $a$ embedded in $L$, and step 2 defines $D_E,D_L$ on those same representatives. For $f:K\to M$ integral naturality reads $D_S(Tf)\beta_M=\beta_KT(D_Rf)$; its image multiplied by $a\in E\subset L$ is the equation for $f\otimes a$. Additivity proves rational naturality. The localized inverse remains inverse. Write $c_{A,B}:TA\widehat\otimes_S^LTB\xrightarrow{\sim}T(A\widehat\otimes_R^LB)$ for the scalar-extension tensor comparison in that lemma's evaluation compatibility. The two supplied integral compatibilities, with all arrows oriented, are
$$\mathrm{ev}_{S,TK}\circ(\beta_K\widehat\otimes1_{TK})=u\circ T(\mathrm{ev}_{R,K})\circ c_{D_RK,K},$$
$$\beta_{D_RK}\circ T(\delta_{R,K})=D_S(\beta_K)\circ\delta_{S,TK}.$$
The first has source $TD_RK\widehat\otimes_S^LTK$ and target $\omega_{X,S}$; the second has source $TK$ and target $D_STD_RK$. For the rational scalar-extension functor $\overline T$, denote the images of $u,c,\beta$ by $\overline u,\overline c,\overline\beta$. Applying $Q_S$ gives, using the tensor and evaluation convention of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom],
$$\mathrm{ev}_{L,\overline TK}\circ(\overline\beta_K\otimes1_{\overline TK})=\overline u\circ\overline T(\mathrm{ev}_{E,K})\circ\overline c_{D_EK,K},$$
$$\overline\beta_{D_EK}\circ\overline T(\delta_{E,K})=D_L(\overline\beta_K)\circ\delta_{L,\overline TK}.$$
These are the required rational evaluation and canonical biduality compatibility equations: $Q_S$ preserves each composite, and $\overline TQ_R=Q_ST$ on the integral arrows occurring here.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3, final sentences: comparison, fractional naturality, and evaluation/biduality compatibility

proof.text:
For $E\subset L\subset M$, write $a_K:T_{M/L}T_{L/E}K\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{M/E}K$ for the integral tensor associator. The composition assertion of [lem-coef-integral-finite-extension] is, with the contravariant direction displayed,
$$\beta_{M/L,T_{L/E}K}\,T_{M/L}(\beta_{L/E,K})=D_{X,\mathcal O_M}(a_K)\,\beta_{M/E,K}\,a_{D_{X,\mathcal O_E}K}.$$
Every factor is integral. Apply $Q_{\mathcal O_M}$: by [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] the functors and factors become exactly the rational scalar-extension functors, comparisons and associators, so the displayed equality is their associator equation. For the identity extension, put $j_K:T_{E/E}K\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ for the integral tensor unit comparison. The supplied integral unit equation is
$$\beta_{E/E,K}=D_R(j_K)\circ j_{D_RK}:T_{E/E}D_RK\longrightarrow D_RT_{E/E}K.$$
Writing $\overline j_K=Q_R(j_K)$, its image is explicitly
$$\overline\beta_{E/E,K}=D_E(\overline j_K)\circ\overline j_{D_EK}.$$
Thus under the specified unit identifications the rational identity-extension comparison is the identity. Because $Q$ preserves identities and composition, these are equations of the specified canonical comparisons, rather than choices of unrelated isomorphisms. This completes all clauses.
